climate_pressure: Coastal flooding, salinity and source-described sea-level pressure around Djobel.
documented_impact: Damage to rice-field/dike systems and pressure to establish safer settlement space.
fcv_mediator: Longstanding contested upland access, unresolved resource rights, limited support and labour constraints.
possible_consequence: The case documents obstacles to safer settlement/adaptation and renewed land tensions; it does not isolate climate change as the origin of the dispute.
alternative_explanations: Longstanding territorial history, state action, resource rights, livelihood dependence and external assistance also shape adaptation and tensions.
uncertainty: Localized historical qualitative evidence; no attribution of the 2017 flood to anthropogenic change, quantified violence trend, or present land adjudication. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Equitable negotiated access, dike maintenance and appropriate technical support are relevant capacities; effectiveness is not established.
compact_statement: In Djobel, flood exposure and pressure to retreat interact with an older upland land dispute that constrains safer settlement; the case is local and multi-causal.
